newsitem.title: BELARUS: Belarus police arrest dozens at protest.
newsitem.headline: Belarus police arrest dozens at protest.

text.p: Belarus police arrested two leading liberal politicians in the former Soviet republic after an unsanctioned protest erupted into clashes on Sunday, and Interfax news agency said a U.S. diplomat was also detained.
The agency quoted police as saying Serzh Alexandrov, first secretary of the U.S. embassy, was among 70 people arrested during a protest against President Alexander Lukashenko.
The United States has become one of Lukashenko's most vociferous opponents.

Special OMON riot police seized Gennady Karpenko, leader of the Civic Union party and deputy head of the former parliament, and his colleague Yuri Zakharenko, a former interior minister, at the party's headquarters, a relative of Karpenko said.
Reuters correspondents saw dozens of arrests being made at the unsanctioned part of the protest, where demonstrators hurled chunks of ice and smashed police car windows.

Police beat protesters with truncheons and there were injuries on both sides as the crowd of about 4,000 nationalists defied a ban on marching and made their way through the city centre towards an authorised rally.
About 10,000 people gathered on Yakob Kolas Square for the sanctioned rally. Scuffles broke out on the edge of the square and at least one on the square itself.

Protesters at the unsanctioned march attacked several police cars, shouting "Belarus into NATO" and "We will not sell our nation's glory" to express their hatred for Lukashenko's policy of forming a union with neighbouring Russia.
The nationalists, waving red and white nationalist flags which Lukashenko has replaced with Soviet emblems, were marking the anniversary of an independent republic created in 1918.
The republic lasted only a few months until it was incorporated by Russian Bolsheviks and Belarus stayed under Moscow rule until the Soviet Union collapsed in 1991.
Unlike people in other former Soviet republics, the majority of the population of 10 million favours closer ties with Moscow.

Sunday's was the latest in a string of protests against Lukashenko, who has cracked down on opposition forces by restricting rallies, arresting protesters and putting a senior opposition leader in prison in recent weeks.
A loose union of prominent politicians, nationalists, intellectuals and students mostly in the capital oppose Lukashenko, who was awarded sweeping powers in a landslide referendum win last November.
Western officials said the vote was illegitimate because Lukashenko ignored the old constitution to push it through.

The United States, one of the most vociferous foreign critics of the former farm chief's increasingly authoritarian rule, said two days ago that it had cut off $40 million in aid to Belarus because of its human rights performance
Interfax said two of three injured policemen were taken to hospital, where one of them was operated on for head injuries.
It quoted police as saying 70 people were arrested.
